silver.note: Aicher's silber. The page ground and the value every foreground is proved against. Authored constant PAPER; painted unchanged.

plane.note: The raised sheet a waiting row, panel or note is printed on. Authored constant PLANE; painted unchanged.

plane-spent.note: SOLVED. The CSS seed --plane-2:#CDD2CE is overwritten at boot by chroma.mix(PAPER, PLANE, 0.35). A done row sits between the ground and the plane so it recedes toward the paper.

ink.note: Near-black with a green cast, never pure black. Body copy, structural rules, the hold button field, the carriage progress bar.

rule.note: SOLVED by inkFor(INK, silver, 3) for non-text boundaries. Lands at 4.69:1, so the same painted value also serves as secondary text (--ink-2 solves identically).

name-ink.note: SOLVED by inkFor(INK, plane, 7). Movement names and primary text inside a waiting row.

channel-pre.note: Channel field, solved by fill(seed, INK, 5.5). Seed already carried ink at 5.77:1, so seed and painted value coincide.

channel-run.note: SOLVED. The seed #2E7CBF fails 5.5:1 against ink and is brightened by fill(); the seed is never painted anywhere in the app.

channel-post.note: Channel field. Seed carried ink at 6.25:1; seed and painted value coincide.

channel-log.note: SOLVED. The seed #7E63A8 is brightened by fill() and is never painted as a field.

channel-settings.note: SOLVED. A channel by mechanism but deliberately the only desaturated one, because settings is not part of the day.

band-pre.note: SOLVED by fill(seed, white, 5.5) for the 132px poster band, where the masthead is knocked out in white. Deep, because the band is the one dark field in the system.

band-run.note: SOLVED for white at 5.5:1. The CSS seed --band:#0A4A80 is overwritten at boot and again on every channel change.

band-post.note: SOLVED for white at 5.5:1. Deep burnt orange, not red: no red is authored anywhere in this system.

band-settings.note: The one case where the seed is painted as the band and solved as the field — the inverse of the four day channels.

display.purpose: The session clock in the carriage and the dial's second-count. The only extended cut in the system, reserved for numerals read at arm's length across a room.

headline.purpose: The movement name in a flooded row. Steps to 22px below 360px.

title.purpose: The movement name at rest, plan titles, the run button. Content voice.

label.purpose: The system's own speaking voice: section markers, headings, button words, the greeting line. Always lowercase.

counter.purpose: Machine metadata: tab counts, step counts, sequence numbers. Always tabular-nums.

fonts.note: Self-hosted variable, preloaded. Stands in for Univers, which is Aicher's face and is not free. The width axis is the part that matters: the 1972 programme is a width/weight matrix, not one cut. font-synthesis:none forbids faking a stop the file does not carry.

shadows.name: rim-hairline
shadows.purpose: Incidental boundary: a waiting or finished row, a chip, a panel. Occupies no space and casts nothing.

shadows.name: rim-structural
shadows.purpose: Structural boundary: the pictogram block's outline, the dial's frame, ghost buttons.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: A flooded row drops its rim entirely. There are no offset or blurred shadows anywhere in this system.

motion.name: state-swap
motion.purpose: Background and colour changes on buttons, tabs and chips.

motion.name: row-restate
motion.purpose: A movement row changing state: background, box-shadow, colour. Height is never animated.

motion.name: spotlight
motion.purpose: Opacity and filter fade when a session starts or ends.

motion.name: carriage-rise
motion.purpose: The session carriage translating up from the bottom edge.

motion.name: row-flip
motion.purpose: The 180-degree Y rotation to a row's demonstration face. Replaced by a face swap under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every transition in the system is switched off and the flip becomes a straight swap.

dimming.name: dim-o
dimming.purpose: Opacity of everything that is not the movement being done, while a session runs.

dimming.name: dim-s
dimming.purpose: Filter applied alongside dim-o. Recedes toward the silver, never toward black.

dimming.name: dim-bg-o
dimming.purpose: Opacity of the poster band during a session.

dimming.name: dim-bg-f
dimming.purpose: Filter on the poster band during a session.

dimming.name: dim-forced-colors
dimming.purpose: Under forced-colors the dimming is switched off entirely: dimming in a user's own two colours destroys legibility rather than focusing it.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.note: max-width. Tightens tab padding; drops the flooded row's headline 26px to 22px and its pictogram 104px to 80px. The only dimensional breakpoint in the file.

breakpoints.name: column
breakpoints.note: The column cap, not a breakpoint. The layout is identical at every width above it; there is no wide-viewport grid on this surface.

contrastTargets.name: primary-text
contrastTargets.where: Movement names on the plane (inkFor(INK, PLANE, 7)).

contrastTargets.name: text
contrastTargets.where: Doses, secondary labels, faded ink on a channel field (fade()).

contrastTargets.name: non-text
contrastTargets.where: Rims, chip outlines, dividers. Solved the same way text is; before this they were picked by eye and landed between 1.26:1 and 1.93:1.

contrastTargets.name: on-channel-field
contrastTargets.where: Anything on a flooded channel band or the poster band, so that a 60%-opacity secondary label still clears the floor on the same field.

raster.head: filled circle, r=4.5
raster.note: One authored pictogram per movement the plan can name, matched longest-key-first on the plan's own wording. The generic figure is the fallback and is itself drawn. OWN-WORLD specified sixteen; the build ships twenty-two and the build wins.

components.name: Pictogram Block
components.description: The 44px square carrying one of twenty-two authored pictograms, drawn on Aicher's raster: strokes at 0/45/90 only, one 4px width throughout, a filled circle for the head. Outlined in the channel while a movement waits; ink-outlined and 104px while it is being done.

narrative.overview:
This is Otl Aicher's 1972 Munich programme applied to a training day. The page is not a stack of cards on a background; it is a sheet of silver paper with bands printed on it. There is no glass, no blur, no lift, no rounded corner and no drop shadow anywhere in the build. What separates one thing from another is a value step, a 1-2px inset rule, and two pixels of bare ground. Everything sits on a 4px unit and a single variable grotesque whose width axis - not its weight - does most of the expressive work.

Two variables carry all the meaning and never trade jobs. Hue names the channel: which part of the day you are looking at. Treatment names the state: outlined is waiting, flooded is happening, receded is finished. A green day and an orange day are the same design proved twice, not two palettes.

The palette itself is the system's real signature: almost nothing in it is authored. Five seeds are pushed through contrast solvers at boot and again on every channel change, and what reaches the screen is the solved output. Two of the four channel seeds never appear on screen at all. The document records what is painted, and names the seed separately where they differ.

The world it refuses is the one this file replaced: translucent violet cards floating over a photograph, with radii and shadows doing the separating.
keyCharacteristics: Silver ground (#D9DDD9), never white, never a dark field
Square corners everywhere - border-radius: 0 without a single exception
4px unit; a 2px gutter of bare ground between adjacent bands
One self-hosted variable font; four width stops (75 / 87 / 100 / 112)
Every colour solved against its ground before it ships, never chosen by eye
No shadows, no blur, no backdrop-filter - inset rules only
22 authored pictograms on a 0/45/90 raster, one per movement
Accessibility branches are designed states, not fallbacks

rules.name: The Solved-Not-Chosen Rule
rules.body: No colour ships as authored. dressPage(), setChannel() and solveStates() push every seed through fill, inkFor and fade - walking the value until it clears its contrast target against its actual ground - and the walked value is what is painted. If a hue cannot carry its type, it is moved until it can; it is never shipped and excused. Record and reuse the painted value, never the seed.

rules.name: The One Channel Rule
rules.body: Exactly one channel hue is on screen at a time. The tab strip is the single licensed exception: it is the one place all four appear at once, because it is the map. Anywhere else, two channel hues in the same viewport means the system is contradicting its own first rule.

rules.name: The No-Red Rule
rules.body: Aicher removed red from the 1972 spectrum and nothing here needs it, because hue names which channel you are in and never how urgent something is. Urgency carries by weight and rule instead: the expired-token line goes to full ink, weight 700, with a 2px underline. No red is authored anywhere in the stylesheet or the app script.

rules.name: The Width-Axis Rule
rules.body: Emphasis moves along the width axis before it moves along weight. Four stops, and each means something: 75% is machine metadata (counts, sequence numbers), 87% is the system's own voice (every label, every button word, every heading), 100% is content (movement names, prose), 112% is the clock. A new size that does not land on one of these four stops is not part of the ramp.

rules.name: The Lowercase Programme Rule
rules.body: Every system label is text-transform: lowercase - the masthead, headings, tabs, buttons, state chips. Content is not: an exercise name keeps the capitals the plan gave it. Lowercase is how the interface signals that it is the interface talking.

rules.name: The Two-Pixel Gutter Rule
rules.body: Adjacent surfaces are separated by 2px of ground, never by a margin and never by a border between them. Bands touch the column edge; the gutter is the only thing between them.

rules.name: The Single Column Rule
rules.body: One 620px column at every width. Do not introduce a wide-viewport grid, a sidebar, or a two-up layout on this surface.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this system casts. If a surface needs to read as separate, give it a value step, an inset rule, or 2px of gutter. A box-shadow with a non-zero offset or blur is a bug in this world, not a style choice.

rules.name: The Three-Value Rule
rules.body: Depth has exactly three positions - plane, ground, spent - and they are already spent. Do not introduce a fourth surface value.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Every corner in this world is square. There is no "just this one" - a single rounded element reads as an element from a different system that wandered in.

rules.name: The Raster Rule
rules.body: Pictograms are drawn on a 44x44 grid using strokes at 0, 45 and 90 degrees only, one 4px stroke width throughout, stroke-linecap: butt, stroke-linejoin: miter, and a filled circle for the head. Twenty-two are authored, one for every movement the plan can name; the generic figure is the fallback and is itself drawn.

dos: Do solve every new colour against its actual ground before shipping it - text at 4.5:1, primary text at 7:1, non-text boundaries at 3:1, and anything on a flooded channel field at 5.5:1. Use fill, inkFor and fade; do not eyeball a value.
Do record and reuse the painted value, never the seed. #2E7CBF and #7E63A8 are inputs to the solver and appear nowhere on screen.
Do put one channel hue on screen at a time, and let the tab strip be the only place all four meet.
Do signal state by treatment - outlined, flooded, receded - and always spell the state out in words as well.
Do move emphasis along the width axis (75 / 87 / 100 / 112) before reaching for another weight.
Do set every system label in lowercase, and leave content's capitals alone.
Do separate surfaces with 2px of bare ground, a value step, or an inset rule.
Do draw new icons and pictograms on the 0/45/90 raster at one 4px stroke width, and give every movement its own.
Do keep touch targets at 44px minimum, 48px for anything used mid-session.
Do ship the reduced-motion, reduced-transparency and forced-colors branches with any new surface. They are part of the design, not a cleanup pass.
donts: Don't add a border-radius. Anywhere. The vocabulary is one value: 0.
Don't add a drop shadow, a blur, or a backdrop-filter. Every shadow in this system is inset 0 0 0 Npx and casts nothing.
Don't introduce red. Hue names the channel, never urgency; urgency carries by weight, full ink, and a rule.
Don't signal state by changing hue, or by colour alone.
Don't put a categorical palette in a chart. Charts are a single-hue ramp of the channel currently on screen.
Don't paint a dark field. The poster band is the one dark thing in the system, and the spotlight recedes toward the silver, never toward black.
Don't let a letter, digit or emoji stand in for a drawn mark.
Don't widen the column past 620px or add a wide-viewport grid to this surface.
Don't invent a type size outside the ramp, and don't let the browser synthesise a weight or width the font file does not carry (font-synthesis: none).
